package_info.why_malicious: These versions of struts2-core contain a critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability (CVSS 9.8) in the HttpParameters class. The flaw arises from improper case normalization of HTTP parameter names, allowing attackers to bypass security controls and inject malicious input. The vulnerability is easily automatable, widely exploitable due to the prevalence of Struts2, and poses a high risk of exploitation, especially during periods of reduced monitoring or staffing.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Processes HTTP parameters without enforcing case normalization or validation, enabling attackers to supply parameter names with varying cases to bypass security checks and reach unsafe code paths.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code directly inserts user-supplied parameter names and values into internal data structures without normalizing case or validating input. This allows attackers to craft parameter names that evade security filters, leading to potential injection of malicious payloads.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Secure parameter handling should strictly validate and normalize parameter names to a canonical form before processing, ensuring that security controls cannot be bypassed by case variations. The actual behavior allows unvalidated, case-variant input to influence application logic.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate code may process HTTP parameters, but must always enforce strict validation and normalization to prevent bypassing of security controls. Direct mapping of user input without such checks is not legitimate.
key_indicators: Absence of case normalization in parameter processing
Direct insertion of user-supplied parameter names into internal maps
Lack of input validation or sanitization on parameter names and values
Parameter names accepted in arbitrary case, enabling filter bypass

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when processing specially crafted HTTP requests with malicious parameters)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Enables an attacker to inject and execute arbitrary commands on the server by exploiting the parameter handling flaw. Crafted HTTP parameters with specific casing can bypass security checks and trigger code execution paths.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The ability to inject arbitrary parameters that are interpreted as code or commands is a hallmark of RCE vulnerabilities. The crafted HTTP request leverages the lack of parameter name normalization to bypass security filters and reach code execution logic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal HTTP parameter handling should never result in user-supplied input being interpreted as executable code or commands. Secure frameworks must ensure that user input cannot directly influence code execution paths.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate use case where user-supplied HTTP parameters should directly trigger command execution on the server. All such input should be strictly validated and never mapped to execution logic.
key_indicators: User-controlled HTTP parameters leading to command execution
Parameter names with unusual or mixed-case variations in requests
Absence of input sanitization or validation in request processing
Observed process execution (e.g., shell commands) triggered by HTTP requests

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a specially crafted HTTP request with malicious parameters using case variations to exploit improper parameter name handling.
attack_chain.leads_to: Bypass of security controls and injection of malicious input into the application.

attack_chain.action: Vulnerable code in HttpParameters.java processes the parameters without proper validation or normalization, allowing the malicious payload to be interpreted by downstream logic.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of attacker-supplied code or commands on the server (remote code execution).

attack_chain.action: Attacker achieves remote code execution on the target system by leveraging the injected payload.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full compromise of the affected server, enabling further malicious activity.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected process execution (e.g., shell commands) triggered by HTTP requests to .action endpoints
HTTP requests containing parameter names with unusual or mixed-case variations
Web application process spawning system or shell processes in response to user input
Application logs showing errors or stack traces referencing HttpParameters or Dispatcher classes during request processing
file_indicators: Presence of struts2-core versions 2.0.0-2.5.2 or 6.0.0-6.3.0.1 in application dependencies
References to org/apache/struts2/dispatcher/HttpParameters.java in deployed code or stack traces
References to vulnerable Struts2 artifacts in dependency manifests (e.g., pom.xml, SBOMs)
network_indicators: Inbound HTTP requests to .action endpoints with suspicious or non-standard parameter casing
POST requests containing parameter names or values matching known exploitation patterns (e.g., cmd=, payloads invoking system commands)
Unusual frequency or patterns of requests with mixed-case parameter names
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor HTTP traffic to .action endpoints for requests with parameter names using mixed or non-standard casing. Inspect application logs for errors or stack traces referencing HttpParameters or Dispatcher classes. Use software composition analysis (SCA) tools and SBOMs to identify the presence of vulnerable struts2-core versions in dependencies. Monitor the web application process for unexpected process execution or network activity, and correlate with incoming HTTP requests containing suspicious parameters.
